metadata.note: Two more pieces of the Erie Railroad system, alongside the main line (erie_railroad_mainline.geojson) and the Salamanca-Dayton broad-gauge extension (atlantic_great_western_jamestown.geojson). The Chicago extension is what actually let the Erie's New York-Chicago named trains (Erie Limited, Lake Cities, Atlantic Express, Pacific Express) live up to their names -- built 1880 as the Chicago & Atlantic Railway (Marion, OH-Hammond, IN, 270 miles), connecting at Marion to another Erie-system component (the New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio) and reaching Chicago itself over the jointly-owned Chicago & Western Indiana Railroad. Reorganized as the Chicago and Erie Railroad after an 1890 bankruptcy, purchased by the Erie Railroad in 1895 (keeping its own corporate name until a 1941 consolidation). The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railway is a separate acquired system: formed Jun 12 1881 from six small New Jersey/Pennsylvania predecessor roads to carry anthracite coal from the Stroudsburg, PA interchange to New York Harbor, with a substantial northern New Jersey commuter passenger business alongside it. The Erie owned the NYS&W 1898-1940, after which it reverted to independent operation -- meaning it was NOT part of the 1960 Erie Lackawanna merger, and its own passenger (including NJ commuter) service outlived the Erie name, continuing until 1966. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: both real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search). The Chicago extension's traced length (268.7 mi) matches the sourced Chicago & Atlantic + Chicago & Western Indiana mileage (270 + 19 = ~268 mi from Marion via Hammond into Chicago) closely, corroborating the routing. The NYS&W traced length (113.3 mi) runs somewhat longer than the sourced 100.7 mi, plausibly reflecting real curves through NJ's dense modern rail network along a still-active short line.

metadata.rule4_split_2026_08_24: Rule 4 ownership split. The Erie Railroad and the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western did not become one another -- they merged on October 17 1960 into a new company, the Erie Lackawanna Railroad (reorganized as the Erie Lackawanna Railway in 1968 under the Dereco holding company, and folded into Conrail April 1 1976). Before this pass the post-1960 years were still drawn in the predecessors' own colours, so one company appeared on the map in two different colours -- ex-Erie segments in Erie black #22223B, ex-Lackawanna in DL&W brown #7F5539. Every feature whose segments ran past 1960 has been split at the merger date into a second feature with identical geometry, company 'Erie Lackawanna Railroad', colour #A02C5A. Six features across six files: erie-mainline-jerseycity-buffalo, dlw-hoboken-scranton-buffalo, erie-salamanca-jamestown-dayton, erie-chicago-extension, erie-buffalo-niagara-falls, cmv-cleveland-youngstown. The NYS&W (nysw-jerseycity-stroudsburg) is deliberately NOT included -- it had reverted to independent operation by 1940 and was not part of the merger.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
